articleTitle: Automatic Segmentation of the Substantia Nigra in Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging of Non-Parkinson and Parkinson's Disease Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: The loss of neurons in the substantia nigra (SN) is a pathological feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), but its segmentation in medical imaging is challenging. This study proposes an automatic method to segment Non-PD and PD patients' left and right SN in susceptibility-weighted images (SWI) and Magnitude SWI-derived images. The images used in this study were obtained from the NTUA Parkinson's disease database: 11 SWI image volumes (4 Non-PD and 7 PD) and 8 Magnitude image volumes (3 Non-PD and 5 PD). One Non-PD template was created per each image type to obtain a mask of the left and right SN. All images were registered to the respective template. The segmentation method consisted of setting a seed point based on the masks of 2D image slices created to perform a flood fill algorithm. The method's performance was evaluated using the dice similarity coefficient (DSC) between automatic and manual segmentation. The segmentation method achieved higher performance using the SWI images (DSC: SN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.684 \pm 0.182$</tex>; left SN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.722 \pm 0.137$</tex>; right SN: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.664 \pm 0.226$</tex>) than using the Magnitude images (DSC: SN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.589 \pm 0.249$</tex>; left SN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.604 \pm 0.223$</tex>; right SN <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.569 \pm$</tex> 0.284), suggesting that the SWI images are more suitable for SN segmentation. Although not yet as effective as manual segmentation, the proposed method may aid in SN segmentation.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Feature Analysis and Machine Learning for Cross-Patient Seizure Type Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Epilepsy, affecting around 70 million people worldwide, is characterized by recurring seizures. EEG plays a crucial role in diagnosis, but manual analysis is time-intensive. Automated methods offer efficiency, aiding seizure analysis. In this study, we introduce a cross-patient six-class seizuretype classification method. Additionally, our research involved analyzing features from various frequency bands and identifying important features for seizure-type classification. This analytical understanding offers a promising path to support researchers in thoroughly investigating different seizure types within EEGs.

articleTitle: Occluded Image Interpretation Ability Assessment Under Different Mental Workloads: An Eye-Tracking Study
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Image interpretation experts play a crucial role in various domains in daily life such as military, healthcare, and education. Accurately assessing an individual's ability to perform such tasks is of great importance. In this study, we designed an image interpretation task with three levels of occlusion, which better reflected the real-world working environments. Using the Eyelink 1000plus eye-tracking system, we collected both behavioral data and eye-tracking data from 64 participants while they performed the image interpretation tasks. Through confirmatory factor analysis, we extracted the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-factor, representing the comprehensive image interpretation ability, from the behavioral performance data of the tasks with different levels of occlusion. We divided all participants into two groups according to their <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>-factors and conducted statistical analyses on their eyetracking data. The results showed that, under all three levels of mental workload, the high-ability group exhibited fewer fixations, saccades, and blinks. Additionally, the high-ability group showed significantly longer fixation duration under the medium and high mental workload conditions. Furthermore, our study also provided a few machine learning algorithms for assessing individuals' image interpretation ability based on eye-tracking features with the highest Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.81.

articleTitle: Insights into the Evolution of GC Content in Coronavirus Genome Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: GC content is an important feature of genomic nucleic acid sequence composition. The change of GC content is closely related to the origin, evolution, and functional variation of the gene. Coronavirus can cause interspecific transmission and pose a serious threat to human and animal health. At present, it has led to three major epidemics that have caused global panic. This paper attempts to systematically analyze the relationship between coronavirus classification and GC content in the genome. Through the reference sequence of coronavirus provided by NCBI, the GC content characteristics of coronavirus were studied by MEGA, Mafft, and other software. The results showed that the GC content of coronavirus was closely related to the hypotype structure, the content was 30%-50%, and some coronaviruses had a certain affinity. In conclusion, this paper provides new insights for understanding the relevant knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 and is helpful to study the pathogenicity and evolutionary mechanism of novel coronavirus.

articleTitle: Optical Detection of the Body Mass Index and Related Parameters Using Multiple Spatially Resolved Reflection Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Obesity is a common problem for many people. In order to assist people combating obesity, providing methods to quickly, easily, and inexpensively assess their body composition is important. This article investigates how noninvasive, optical sensors based on multiple spatially resolved reflection spectroscopy can be used to measure the body mass index and body composition parameters. Using machine learning to train continuous feature networks, it is possible to predict the body mass index of a subject, with a correlation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=0.61$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p<0.0001$</tex>. Similarly, the predicted body mass index shows correlations to both the subject's visceral fat <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R=0.44, p=0.0023)$</tex> and skeletal muscle mass index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R=0.52, p=0.0003)$</tex>, indicating that the trained neural network is capable of identifying both types of tissue. Strategies to independently detect either type of tissue are discussed.

articleTitle: Oral Health Parameter-Based Mini-Mental State Examination Indication Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Among the growing elderly population, the number of people with neurocognitive disease increases, highlighting the need for early diagnosis. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) is one of the tools used to diagnose neurocognitive disease. The existence of a relationship between degraded oral health and decreased MMSE scores is known. Using machine Learning (ML) techniques, the present study aimed to study the potential of using oral health and demographic examination data to indicate the level of MMSE score. Data from a study evaluating oral health over time and data from an ongoing study evaluating the general health in an elderly population were used as inputs to ML models Random Forest (RF), Support Vektor Machine (SVM), and Catboost (CB) for the binary indication of MMSE score 30 or MMSE score 26 or lower was used to find the best classification performance to distinguish between MMSE low and healthy control (HC) groups. The classifiers were trained using the nested cross-validation (nCV) method to mitigate the risk of overfiting. CB and RF achieved the highest classification accuracy of 80%. However, the CB classifier outperformed other classifiers with 76.4 average accuracies over all the nCV combinations. The oral health parameters and demographics used as input to the ML classifiers carry enough information to distinguish between MMSE low and HC groups. This study suggests that oral health examination might provide information that can be used with the help of Machine Learning (ML) to indicate lowered MMSE scores.

articleTitle: Efficient Methods to Generate NIPT Male Samples with Aberrations on Sex Chromosomes for Benchmarking NIPT Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Noninvasive prenatal test (NIPT) has become a routine screening method to detect autosomal chromosomal aberrations. Predicting sex chromosome aneuploidies (SCAs) is more difficult due to the complicated genomic characteristics of sex chromosomes. Benchmarking the sensitivity of NIPT algorithms is challenging due to the lack of positive samples. In this paper, we introduce simple and efficient computational methods to create aberrations on sex chromosomes for NIPT male samples (i.e., creating male samples with XXY or XYY aberrations) from negative NIPT samples. We applied the methods to create 513 positive samples with XXY aberrations and 200 positive samples with XYY aberrations to evaluate the sensitivity of three NIPT algorithms WisecondorX, its improvement VINIPT, and CNVkit. Experiements on both negative and positive samples showed that the algorithms have high sensitivity in detecting XXY and XYY aberrations (100% for WisecondorX and VINIPT; and 99.2% for CNVkit). The VINIPT algorithm has an overall specificity of 99.8% and better than WisecondorX (∼96.8%) and CNVkit (∼99%). The results indicate that VINIPT can play as a powerful tool for screening aberrations on sex chromosomes of male samples.

articleTitle: An Efficient Computational Method to Create Positive NIPT Samples with Autosomal Trisomy
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Noninvasive prenatal test (NIPT) has been widely used for screening trisomy on chromosomes 13 (T13), 18 (T18), and 21 (T21). However, the false negative rate of NIPT algorithms has not been thoroughly evaluated due to the lack of positive samples. In this study, we present an efficient computational approach to create positive samples with autosomal trisomy from negative samples. We applied the approach to establish a low coverage dataset of 1440 positive samples with T13, T18, and T21 aberrations for both mosaic and non-mosaic conditions. We examined the performance of WisecondorX and its improvement, called VINIPT, on both negative and positive datasets. Experiments showed that WisecondorX and VINIPT were able to detect all non-mosaic samples with T13, T18, and T21 aberrations (i.e., the sensitivity of 100%). When analyzing mosaic samples, both WisecondorX and VINIPT have the overall sensitivity of 99.7% on detecting T13, T18, and T21 aberrations from mosaic samples. WisecondorX has the specificity of 98.5% for the nonmosaic analysis, but a considerably lower specificity of 95% for the mosaic analysis. VINIPT has a much better specificity than WisecondorX, i.e., 99.9% for the non-mosaic analysis, and 98.2% for the mosaic analysis. The results suggest that VINIPT can play as a powerful tool for detecting autosomal trisomy from the low coverage data.

articleTitle: A Prototype System Design for Identification and Classification of Stimulation Sites Inducing Hand Motor Function
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: To address the challenges of surface electrical stimulation using large electrodes, which are not capable of selectively activating muscles and may induce varying muscle responses with variations in body posture, this study proposed a system including hardware platform and a PC software, which can identify and classify stimulation sites. The system's hardware platform is a surface functional electrical stimulation (FES) device with array electrodes, while the PC software is used for stimulation parameter configuration and limb movement trajectory data acquisition based on Leap Motion and ESP8266. To test the system's performance, wrist extension and flexion movements were performed. The results demonstrate that the system can establish parameters for stimulation sites in the array electrodes and capture the motion trajectories of wrist extension and wrist flexion in real-time during limb movement. This system establishes a platform for creating a database of limb movement trajectories and identifying and categorizing stimulation sites for target movements in various body postures using deep learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Identification of Pyroptosis-Related Gene Functions in Psoriasis and Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Using Gene Regulatory Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Pyroptosis, a form of programmed cell death, plays a pivotal role in various physiological and pathological processes, including autoimmune diseases like psoriasis and cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE). This study aims to analyze the expression patterns of pyroptosis-related genes in psoriasis and CLE using gene profiling techniques, exploring their roles in the onset and progression of these diseases, and identifying potential therapeutic drugs. We acquired gene expression datasets of psoriasis and CLE patients, both from lesional and nonlesional skin areas, using the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus database. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were selected using the limma algorithm, followed by enrichment analysis of these DEGs with WebGestalt. Pyroptosis-related genes were collected to construct transcriptional regulatory networks using GENIE3, and the DGIdb database was used to predict potential therapeutic drugs. We found that psoriasis and CLE patients share pyroptosis genes, including CHMP7 and CASP8. Psoriasis DEGs are involved in biological processes such as cell migration, proliferation, and signal transduction regulation, while CLE DEGs involve immune response, defense mechanisms, and immune system regulation. In the transcriptional regulatory network, transcription factors such as STAT3, VD3, and MYC play key regulatory roles and are potential therapeutic targets. Drugs like Cyclosporine and Methotrexate can target these factors for treatment. Together, this work investigated the mechanisms and biological processes common and distinct in psoriasis and CLE, revealing the regulatory function of pyroptosis in these diseases and providing new insights and methods for their treatment.

articleTitle: SSGCN: A Spatial Domain Identification Framework Based on Graph Convolutional Neural Network with Adaptively Reweighting Edges
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Leveraging spatial location and gene expression of spots for spatial domain identification through spatial transcriptomics data is important for understanding the tissue heterogeneity, and comprehending developmental processes. In this study, we propose a spatial domain identification framework SSGCN based on graph neural network, which fully considers spatial locations and similarity between spots according to their gene expression. Specifically, SSGCN takes spatial location and gene expression as input, reassigns edges' weights of graph by calculating the expression similarity between nodes, and ultimately learns a low-dimensional representation for spatial domain assignment. We conduct extensive experiments on four datasets from various platforms with different resolutions. The experimental results show that SSGCN is superior to other spatial clustering methods, and also demonstrate its cross-platform applicability.

articleTitle: Research on Classification Method of Infectious Diseases in Population Mobility Based on Bipartite Interactive Graph Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: The high contagiousness of COVID-19 brings great challenges to epidemic prevention. This article aims to explore how to use advanced graph neural network technology to effectively classify infectious diseases in the context of population mobility. The article first constructs a spatio-temporal adjacency matrix that reflects the characteristics of population mobility, in which nodes represent geographical areas and edge weights represent the intensity of population mobility between different regions. Subsequently, combined with the characteristics of the spread of infectious diseases, a deep learning model for such structured data - a two-part interactive graph neural network algorithm network - was designed and trained. Specifically, we first build a complete graph data according to users and their travel locations, which contains specific user groups and their historical travel records. Then, two interactive graph neural network algorithms are designed for this graph to capture the travel records of different users and their spatial interactions, and classify the crowd according to the node embeddings learned by the model, to identify groups that may be infected. Finally, the superiority of the method is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: On an Approach to the Study of Distances Between DNA Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: We are considering an approach to the study of the proximity of genomes. The approach is based on the definition and consideration of a triangular norm (triangular badness) for the distances between genomes and, based on it, the norm for the corresponding distance matrices. We used mtDNA in our research, and of the algorithms for comparing genomes, first of all, the Needleman - Wunsch algorithm algorithm (metric). However, the approach can be applied to any relevant genome regions and any described algorithms for calculating the proximity of strings. As results, we obtained, among other things, a comparison of variants of different metrics between genomes, the results of reconstruction of partially filled distance matrices, the description of the application of the pair correlation method for the sequences of badness of the triangles of distance matrices, as well as descriptions of possible generalizations for various similar problems.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Double-Layer Multiple Instance Learning Algorithm for Whole Slide Image Classification of Primary Gastric Lymphoma
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Primary Gastric Lymphoma (PGL) is a type of malignant lymphoma that originates in the stomach. Timely and precise diagnosis and classification are crucial for effective treatment and predicting outcomes. Advances in artificial intelligence, especially deep learning, have ushered in a new era for medical diagnostics. Weakly supervised learning, in particular, is gaining traction for classifying histopathological whole slide images (WSIs). Nonetheless, there remain challenges, such as the classification of small sample cohorts. To address these issues, we propose a novel multi-scale double-layer multiple instance learning classification algorithm for accurate classification of PGL. This algorithm leverages pseudo-bags-a technique to effectively augment the sample size-and employs multiple instance learning to distill essential features. It then constructs an enhanced classification model utilizing a multi-scale, double-layer approach. Validation using clinical pathological data indicates that our method outperforms other latest methods in classifying primary gastric lymphoma, as well as obtains superior results on the CAMELYON-16 dataset. Our framework holds promise for broader adoption across various medical applications.

articleTitle: NFC-Based Healthcare Information System: Enhancing Accessibility and Efficiency of Medical Data Management for Patients and Healthcare Personnel
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Near-field communication (NFC) technology garnered attention in healthcare, promising to transform practices, especially in managing patient records. This study explored NFC's potential in revolutionizing medical document management, addressing limitations in current record-keeping systems: inadequate accessibility, security loopholes, and interoperability challenges in paper-based and electronic medical records. The research examined NFC's past feasibility as a robust platform for securely storing medical documents, identifying essential technical requirements for integration and functionality. The study collaborated closely with healthcare facilities, understanding past needs and challenges in implementing NFC-based solutions and evaluating user acceptance. The conceptual framework centered on past patient-centricity, universal usability, stringent data security measures, and seamless NFC integration with existing healthcare systems. Methodologically, the study involved past phases: interviews for insights, identification of suitable NFC technology, software development, and deploying the NFC-based Healthcare Information System. Challenges in past real-world clinical testing limited direct feedback due to privacy regulations, but internal testing facilitated refinements, enhancing the system's past functionality and user-friendliness. Ultimately, past findings aimed to provide comprehensive guidelines for leveraging NFC's potential in the past, revolutionizing medical document management. Lakambin-E's system highlighted NFC's benefits, promising streamlined data accessibility, enhanced medical processes, and improved patient care in the healthcare ecosystem.

articleTitle: Cross-Task Joint Network for Detecting Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction and Estimating Ejection Fraction from Electrocardiograms
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is an advanced-stage manifestation of various heart diseases and seriously threatens human health. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is a key clinical indicator for diagnosing HFrEF and measuring its severity. Existing deep learning methods can quickly detect HFrEF from electrocardiograms (ECGs), but cannot simultaneously provide clinicians or patients with specific LVEF values to assess severity. In this paper, we developed a novel cross-task joint network (CTJNet) using multi-channel ECGs, which could not only detect HFrEF and estimate specific LVEF values to measure its severity, but also effectively utilize the correlations between the above two tasks to improve performance. Specifically, we first designed a two-stage architecture for the CTJNet consisting of a channel-specific stage and a task-specific stage. In the channel-specific stage, we proposed a cross-task dualconstraint mechanism to enable the feature representations extracted from each channel ECG to have good generality across different tasks. For the task-specific stage, we developed a crosstask interaction mechanism to better share information across tasks by learning inter-task correlations. Experimental results showed that compared with the existing state-of-the-art methods, the CTJNet improved the average accuracy of HFrEF detection by at least 4.05% and reduced the mean absolute error of LVEF estimation by at least 9.85%. Meanwhile, the CTJNet also outperformed single-task learning methods, indicating that it could effectively utilize inter-task correlations. These results demonstrated the good potential of our method for clinical applications in HFrEF detection and LVEF estimation.

Author Keywords: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

articleTitle: Brain Malignant Tumor Classification Using MRI Scans and Optimized CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Based on Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures with optimized hyperparameters, this study proposes a machine learning system for classification of brain malignant tumors. Using a two-level approach, the first level identifies the most suitable MRI modalities for classification by evaluating the performance of the modalities under different hyperparameters. The second level consists of the development and comparison of two CNN architectures, Inceptionv3 and DenseNet121, based on their respective training methods. As part of the optimization process, various hyperparameters are tested, such as epochs, batch sizes, learning rates, and dropout rates. Additionally, it was found that learning rate has an important impact on the training phase with a lower learning rate resulting in a smoother, more consistent process. As a result of optimizing the system, it has been demonstrated that it can accurately classify brain malignant tumors, particularly Glioblastomas.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation Index System for Multi-Dimensional Cognitive Impairment Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a cognitive disorder, which is more common in the elderly. With the increasing number of the elderly, it is quite necessary to screen the cognitive impairment of the elderly. Compared with the conventional, more laborious single-task methods, we have merged multiple speaking tasks including Picture Description Task (PDT), Five-Word Test (FWT), and Clock Drawing Test (CDT). This integration allows for extracting 319 pertinent features from subjects' vocal output, ASR transcribed texts, and track maps. Subsequently, we screened these features and determined their weights, culminating in the development of a comprehensive evaluation index system. This system includes dimensions of language, memory, execution and visual-spatial, is designed to examine the cognitive ability of the subjects. The F1 value of the binary classification task of healthy control (HC) people and patients with cognitive impairment (CI) was 80.86%, which increased by 1.57% compared with the other best method XGBoost. With our comprehensive evaluation index system, we can more comprehensively and quickly carry out early cognitive impairment screening and clinical research.

articleTitle: ADNPPro: Enhanced Promoter Prediction in Nannochloropsis Using Attention-Based Densenet
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Nannochloropsis is a significant genus of marine microalgae, renowned for its strain diversity and high productivity. However, it faces challenges in achieving optimal yields using wild-type strains and traditional cultivation methods. Promoters play a crucial role in regulating gene expression, but current algorithms for recognizing Nannochloropsis promoters have limitations in accuracy and interpretability. To address this problem, we introduce ADNPPro (Attention-based DenseNet Predict Promoter), merging an attention mechanism with a densely connected convolutional neural network. By interpreting the deep learning model, we process an integrated analysis of sequence importance scores, enabling a deeper understanding of key promoter features across various Nannochloropsis strains. Experimental results demonstrate the robust generalization capability of ADNPPro across six Nannochloropsis strains. Motif analysis provides insights into their diverse performance capabilities and enhances the understanding of Nannochloropsis promoter characteristics. The introduction of this framework is set to advance synthetic biology, offering insights into the biological significance of sequence features.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Framework with Multimodal Molecular Representation for Molecular Property Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Molecular property prediction is a basic research problem in the field of drug design and discovery. Effective molecular representation can help models accurately predict the properties of molecules. To capture the physical-chemical properties of molecular fingerprint, the functional group information of molecular fragment and the structural features of molecular graph. This paper first combined molecular fragment and molecular graph representation to extract local and global features of molecules. Then, molecular fingerprint was added to the graph representation to achieve a combination of multi-modal representation. And applied the method to establish a molecular property prediction model, called PFG. To evaluate the PFG model, experiments were conducted on 10 benchmark datasets applying the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) evaluation indicators. Compared with models based only on fingerprint or graph representation, the model achieved better prediction results on 9 datasets. The effectiveness of the combined molecular representation method proposed in this paper was verified. Compared with SVM, GBDT, RF, XGBoost, GAT, Attention FP, DMPNN, FP-GNN and FraGAT models, the effectiveness of the proposed method is proved.

articleTitle: An Integrated Genomics Workflow Tool: Simulating Reads, Evaluating Read Alignments, and Optimizing Variant Calling Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)
abstract: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) is a pivotal technique in genome sequencing due to its high throughput, rapid results, cost-effectiveness, and enhanced accuracy. Its significance extends across various domains, playing a crucial role in identifying genetic variations and exploring genomic complexity. NGS finds applications in diverse fields such as clinical genomics, comparative genomics, functional genomics, and metagenomics, contributing substantially to advancements in research, medicine, and scientific disciplines. Within the sphere of genomics data science, the execution of read simulation, mapping, and variant calling holds paramount importance for obtaining precise and dependable results. Given the plethora of tools available for these purposes, each employing distinct methodologies and options, a nuanced understanding of their intricacies becomes imperative for optimization. This research, situated at the intersection of data science and genomics, involves a meticulous assessment of various tools, elucidating their individual strengths and weaknesses through rigorous experimentation and analysis. This comprehensive evaluation has enabled the researchers to pinpoint the most accurate tools, reinforcing the alignment between the established workflow and the demonstrated efficacy of specific tools in the context of genomics data analysis. To meet these requirements, “VarFind”, an open-source and freely accessible pipeline tool designed to automate the entire process has been introduced (VarFind GitHub repository: VarFinder.)

articleTitle: Neuro-Degenerative Disorder Prediction Using Curated Short Mutated Genome Sequences Through Hybrid Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (ICBCB)

authors.preferredName: L V S K B Kasyap Varanasi
authors.firstName: L V S K B Kasyap

abstract: Psychological disorders are a range of conditions characterized by significant disruptions in a person's thoughts, emotions, and behavior. The WHO reports that over a billion people worldwide have neurological illnesses, and ineffective diagnostics hinder treatment. Mental health disorders continue to be a pervasive global health concern, necessitating innovative early detection and intervention approaches. The classical methods often rely on expensive clinical diagnoses and computational techniques in genome-wide association studies (GWAS) that can be time-consuming. We curate the short genome sequence data for five disorders of fixed and variable lengths through two novel approaches to address these limitations. To our knowledge, this is the first work that suggests extracting short genetic sequences for psychiatric disorders. We investigate different deeplearning (DL) techniques to predict mental health disorders based on the prepared datasets. Our study aims to enhance the accuracy and timeliness of mental health assessments, potentially revolutionizing mental health care delivery. The classification accuracies for the proposed graph neural network with HMM representation on fixed length genome sequence were as follows: SCZ=80%; BP=71% which is the highest when compared to the other DL models. The outcomes of our research reveal promising results, with the curated short genome sequences significantly contributing to identifying mental health disorders. The proposed data curation approaches lay a solid basis for the adoption of DL based mental health prediction tools in healthcare systems. The model encourages early intervention and ultimately improves patient outcomes.
